question: Magnification produced by a lens is equal to:
solution:
The correct answer is __**v/u**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The magnification (m) produced by a lens is given by the formula **m = v/u**, where **v** is the **image distance **and **u** is the **object distance**.
 
• If the image is formed on the same side as the object (**virtual image**), **v** will be **negative**, and if the image is formed on the opposite side (**real image**), **v** will be **positive**.
 
• The magnification can also indicate the nature of the image: if **|m| > 1**, the image is **magnified**; if **|m| 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• For a convex lens, when the object is placed beyond the focal point, the image formed is real and inverted, and the magnification is positive.
 
• For a concave lens, the image formed is always virtual, upright, and diminished, and the magnification is negative.
 
• The **lens formula**, which relates the object distance (u), image distance (v), and focal length (f) of the lens, is given by **1/f = 1/v - 1/u**.
 
• Understanding the sign conventions is crucial for correctly applying these formulas in lens problems.
